guide.p: Work comes up in Part 1 ('Do you work or study?'), Part 2 (a job, a goal, a busy time) and Task 2 (job satisfaction, working hours, automation, unemployment). These words let you speak about your own job and about the labour market in general.

bullets: Learn words in phrases, not alone: notice which verbs, adjectives and prepositions go with them.
Practise each word in a sentence about your own life or country — it will be easier to use in Speaking.
In Writing, choose the precise word over the impressive-sounding one. Accuracy beats complexity.

guide.tip: 'Work' as a noun is uncountable ('I have a lot of work'); 'job' is countable ('She has two jobs').

vocab.meaning: a person who works for a company or organisation
vocab.example: The firm has 300 employees.

vocab.meaning: a person or company that employs people
vocab.example: Employers value good communication skills.

vocab.meaning: a person you work with
vocab.example: I usually have lunch with my colleagues.

vocab.meaning: all the people who work in a company or country
vocab.example: Women now make up half of the workforce.

vocab.meaning: the feeling of enjoying your job
vocab.example: Job satisfaction matters more to me than salary.

vocab.meaning: a healthy division of time between work and personal life
vocab.example: Flexible hours improve work-life balance.

vocab.meaning: arrangements that let employees choose when or where they work
vocab.example: Many parents prefer flexible working.

vocab.meaning: a move to a higher position
vocab.example: She got a promotion after two years.

vocab.meaning: the series of jobs a person has during their working life
vocab.example: Teaching was not my original career path.

vocab.meaning: an official record of a skill or course completed
vocab.example: The job requires a nursing qualification.

vocab.meaning: a period of work, often unpaid, to gain experience
vocab.example: He did a summer internship at a bank.

vocab.meaning: working for several clients rather than one employer
vocab.example: Many designers work freelance.

vocab.meaning: working for yourself rather than an employer
vocab.example: Being self-employed means no fixed income.

vocab.meaning: the state of having no job; the number of people without jobs
vocab.example: Youth unemployment remains high.

vocab.meaning: no longer employed because the job is no longer needed
vocab.example: Two hundred workers were made redundant.

vocab.meaning: fixed yearly pay, usually paid monthly
vocab.example: The starting salary is quite low.

vocab.meaning: pay calculated by the hour, day or week
vocab.example: The minimum wage rose this year.

vocab.meaning: extra benefits in addition to pay
vocab.example: Free lunches are one of the perks of the job.

vocab.meaning: the time by which something must be done
vocab.example: We worked late to meet the deadline.

vocab.meaning: the amount of work a person has to do
vocab.example: Teachers complain about their heavy workload.

vocab.meaning: exhaustion caused by long-term stress at work
vocab.example: Long hours can lead to burnout.

vocab.meaning: how much work is produced in a period of time
vocab.example: Shorter meetings can increase productivity.

vocab.meaning: a person who starts their own business
vocab.example: Young entrepreneurs often start online businesses.

vocab.meaning: to travel regularly between home and work; the journey
vocab.example: My commute takes forty minutes each way.
